notes: Generated by tools/tubuild.py create, then reconciled to shared declarations, eager ROM-order emission, one source-level destructor, real Cup state member methods, and the adjacent factory tail.
The eight State* names are explicit class-anchored inferences from PMF order and behavior; the ROM proves their class identity and order, not their exact original source spelling.

Focused verification is 32/32. The former nine-word StateShuffle residual was NOT scratch-register encoding, as an earlier note in this file claimed. Six of the nine words were a different addressing-mode shape: the ROM re-materialises `this + 0x5400` at the read-modify-write site and addresses through [rN,#0x5c] / [rN,#0x5e], while the reconstruction cached that base in a local (`char *state = c + 0x5400;`) and then CSEd the FIELD address into [rN,#0]. `#pragma opt_common_subs off` is in force over this function and cannot undo it, because the CSE was performed by the source, not by the optimizer. TWO source-level edits close it, both inside the `uu == 0x8000 ... else if` block. An earlier revision of this note said THREE and listed a `vv = -vv;` statement split as the second; that claim is WITHDRAWN -- re-measured by removal on the promoted tree, fusing it into the store as `*(s16*)(c + 0x545e) = -speed;` still gives 32/32 MATCH, so it buys no bytes and is kept split for readability only. The two that do close it: (1) drop the cached base at the store site and respell the full offsets `c + 0x545c` / `c + 0x545e`, which makes mwcc re-materialise `add rN, r4, #0x5400`; (2) spell the increment as a plain read-modify-write (`*(u16*)(c + 0x545c) = *(u16*)(c + 0x545c) + 0x8000;`) rather than `+= 0x8000`, because compound assignment is exactly what makes mwcc CSE the field address. The two loads earlier in the same block KEEP the cached `state` base -- the ROM shares one base register across them. Measured, not reasoned: cached-base + compound += gives 9 differing words; a `(long long)(int)` launder through the full offset gives 0x728 (eight bytes over, it forces a literal-pool address); a freshly declared inner base local plus a plain RMW gives 6; the form above gives 0. RE-MEASURED BY THE BUILDER STAGE, each by removing the spelling and re-running tools/tubuild.py verify on the promoted tree: dropping the re-materialised base gives 31/32 with `1 reloc destination(s) WRONG (sCupShuffleOffsetsY != 0x0213c084:ov006)` and objisolate FAIL; the compound `+= 0x8000` gives 31/32; the statement split gives 32/32, i.e. no effect.

The same edits were applied to the legacy shard src/func_ov006_020df5b8.c, which had never carried a `complete` marker in config/arm9/overlays/ov006/delinks.txt. It compiled to 0x728 bytes before and byte-matches at 0x720 after (tools/match.py, 2004/b56), so the marker was added before the shard was superseded by this TU.

Why every claim in this file is now phrased as a removal measurement: this TU sat shadowed for months partly because the pre-promotion manifest described StateShuffle's residual as 'scratch-register encoding differences' with seven lever families exhausted -- a hypothesis written as a measurement, and wrong. The replacement note then over-claimed one of its own three fixes in the same way, caught by review. Do not add a load-bearing claim here that was not produced by deleting the spelling and re-running the gate.

Issue #2492 continues the promoted TU from PR #2348 and historical scout #2343. CUP-01 replaces the two fake Obj slot-18 self-calls with real virtual OnYoshiTryEat calls. CUP-02 corrects the actual dScMgCup_c PMF receiver and seven own slots (0, 6, 9, 16, 17, 18, 20). CUP-03 corrects the no-inferred-names policy and live-pad prose without changing layout. The scout facts retain their original input/status and measurements; their old field-naming policy does not prohibit honestly inferred or offset-named members with fresh proof. CUP-03 typed fields and CUP-06 lifecycle/components remain reconstruction work; CUP-04 initializes cup on every incoming epilogue path with the measured 0xa4-byte form; hoisting the assignment or using i directly gives 0xa0 bytes. CUP-05 minigame slot-20 int fallthrough remains an unresolved correctness finding. This continuation does not claim whole-source acceptance or new data/BSS ownership. The expanded follow-up after independent rework resolves CUP-05 coherently across the five minigame headers and definitions, preserving the separate actor contract. CUP-03-P corrects the component boundary and live tail-byte claims without layout changes; SOUND-PROV01, TERESA-PROV01 and BASE-PROV01 correct the reviewed dependency prose. Full original-base consumer/TU/metadata and packed-ROM proof is recorded in notes/agents/handoffs/issue-2492-cup-source-review.md. The preceding open-CUP-05 statement describes the preserved first checkpoint.
